newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai finance merger said on track, completed soon.
newsitem.headline: Thai finance merger said on track, completed soon.

text.p: Thailand's biggest merger of financial institutions, between Thai Danu Bank and Finance One Plc, is on track and should be concluded next week, a Thai Danu official said on Wednesday.

"The boards of Finance One and Thai Danu are scheduled to hold meetings on May 15 to approve the merger after the due diligence is completed," Chaiwat Utaiwan, executive vice-president of Thai Danu, told a news conference.
Chaiwat made the comments after rumours and media reports suggested the merger was in danger of collapsing. They said Thai Danu might walk away from the deal because of various problems.
But Thai Danu officials have said the reports and subsequent market rumours were caused by a misunderstanding of the reason behind a two-week extension of the due diligence period.

Chaiwat refused to directly comment on any of the talk that the merger might collapse, saying only boards of directors and shareholders had final say in the merger and it was their decision to approve or reject it.
When asked if Thai Danu would have problems if the merger were not approved, Chaiwat said there would be no "significant damage" and said Thai Danu would continue its normal business.
Chaiwat said the two companies hope trading will resume in their shares on May 16.
"We will submit the resolutions of the board (made on May 15) to the Stock Exchange. We hope both shares will resume trading the following day," he said.
Trading in shares of both companies have been halted since March 3 when they first began talking publicly of the merger.

Senior Finance One officials were not available for comment. But a Finance One public relations officer said Chaiwat had been appointed by both firms to head the merger plan and was the sole person authorised to make joint public statements.

Analysts have said Finance One -- formerly Thailand's largest finance company -- sought the merger because it faced liquidity problems which emerged during a major shakeup of the country's troubled finance sector.

The plans set in motion a spate of proposed mergers between several of Thailand's troubled finance and securities firms. Analysts say the process is just the start of a major shake-up among the country's 91 finance and securities firms.
The industry is suffering from declining loan portfolio quality, high financing costs and losses due to the depressed bourse.
"Thai Danu won't be affected much if the deal fails," said an analyst at Ekachart Finance and Securities.
"But the market is concerned other financial institutions would be hurt by Finance One's inability to pay back loans because Finance One really has liquidity problem," he added.
Finance One has a total of 66 billion baht in outstanding loans. Chaiwat said 20 billion of that is in the troubled property sector and 15 billion in car hire purchase loans.
Thai Danu will take only six billion baht of Finance One's existing property loans, he said.
"The new Thai Danu Bank will need to have a clean loan portfolio to ensure its stability...in the future," he said.
Thai Danu will also sell off Finance One's hire purchase loan portfolio because existing regulations bar commercial banks from the hire purchase business, he said. ($1 = 26 baht)
